title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich Bank 2
plain: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 2 (the side of the engine opposite cylinder 1) shows the engine has been running too rich for the computer's fine-tuning to fix. This usually points to a problem before the converter, such as a leaking injector or high fuel pressure.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible rotten egg smell from the exhaust

causes.name: Faulty upstream or downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Fix any other fuel trim, misfire or O2 sensor codes first
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of and around the O2 sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings and fuel trims
fix: Find and repair the rich running cause first; replace the downstream O2 sensor or catalytic converter only after testing.

title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
plain: The diesel exhaust treatment system (SCR) on bank 1 isn't cutting NOx pollution as much as it should. Bad DEF fluid, a faulty NOx sensor or a worn SCR catalyst are typical reasons.
symptoms: DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Poor quality, diluted or old DEF fluid

checks: Check DEF quality with a refractometer
Compare upstream and downstream NOx sensor readings
Run a DEF dosing test and inspect the injector
fix: Fix DEF quality, sensor or injector problems first; replace the SCR catalyst only after testing.
examples: Frequently seen on modern diesel pickups such as Ram Cummins, Ford Power Stroke and GM Duramax
